podcast.title: "Lost" as a Top 40 Hit
podcast.body: The Puerto Rican boy band Menudo recorded the song "Lost," which was originally intended for Bruno Mars and Philip Lawrence, and it subsequently cracked the Top 40 on Billboard's pop radio chart. Mars and Lawrence sold the song to Menudo for $20,000, a deal that allowed them to remain in LA and helped establish their reputation as hit songwriters. "Menudo's version of Lost cracked the top 40 on Billboard's pop radio chart."

podcast.title: Formation and US Success
podcast.body: Menudo formed in 1977, but their major breakthrough and widespread recognition in the US came later, in the 1980s. "Menudo formed in 1977 even though they did not become a big hit in the US until the 1980s."

podcast.title: Former Member Replaced Lenny Kravitz
podcast.body: A former member of the Puerto Rican boy band Menudo notably replaced Lenny Kravitz in one of his bands, indicating an unexpected connection between the two artists' career paths. "A former Menudo member replaced Lenny Kravitz in one of his bands."

podcast.title: Ricky Martin's Early Career
podcast.body: Ricky Martin, who later achieved solo international stardom, began his career with Menudo when he was 12 years old. "Ricky Martin was 12 when he started with Menudo."
